what_happened.line: After a long hearing, the Conservation Commission continued the fire road violation at a lakeside property and told the applicant to resubmit a corrected plan.
The resubmission must include an as-built of the whole driveway, regrading to the approved plan, revised plantings and a floodplain compensation area.
The commission voted negative determinations for 568 Reservoir Road and 379 Townsend Harbor Road, and approved an order of conditions for the 160 Mass Ave culvert.
It continued the 260 warehouse, 411 Goodrich Street and 205 Sunset Lane filings to June 1st, and the agent was to look into a third-party wetland review of the warehouse.
Votes closed out the 192 Townsend Harbor Road enforcement, issued two certificates of compliance and held a third; the agent, Matt Morrow, retired and Nadia takes over.

why_it_matters: Wetland rulings decide what neighbors and owners near water, such as the lakeside site and the Townsend Harbor Road drainage, may build and must fix, and a continued violation stays unresolved until the commission accepts a revised plan.
Handing the agent role to a new person changes who handles day-to-day filings and site checks for applicants and neighbors.
watch_next: June 1st meeting: continued hearings for the warehouse, 411 Goodrich Street and 205 Sunset Lane, which also owes a plan of what exists versus what was approved.
The next meeting: review of the lakeside violation's as-built, remediation plan, plantings and floodplain compensation.
